test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Choose the correct meaning of Idiom "Hoist with one's own petard".

options.text: Fall victim to one's own plan

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Fall victim to one's own plan**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Hoist with one's own petard"** originates from Shakespeare's play "Hamlet" and means to suffer harm or be defeated by one's own plan or actions. (अपने ही योजना से नुकसान उठाना) • **Example:** The corrupt politician was hoist with his own petard when his fraudulent activities were exposed. • In this context, the correct meaning is **"Fall victim to one's own plan"**, which perfectly explains the situation where someone is harmed by the very scheme they intended for someone else. (अपने ही योजना से नुकसान होना) • **Example:** The hacker tried to exploit a system but was hoist with his own petard when his own computer got infected. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Fall victim to one's own plan**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Succeed through betrayal** (धोखे से सफलता हासिल करना): Refers to achieving success by deceiving or betraying someone. • **Example:** He succeeded through betrayal, deceiving his business partner to gain full control of the company. • **Win by surprise** (आश्चर्य से जीतना): Refers to gaining victory unexpectedly or by catching someone off guard. • **Example:** The underdog team won by surprise in the final match, leaving everyone astonished. • **Escape punishment cleverly** (चतुराई से सजा से बचना): Refers to avoiding consequences or punishment through wit and cleverness. • **Example:** The cunning thief escaped punishment cleverly by providing false evidence. bc:Tae3, The correct answer is: **Pantheism**.
